topline.text: A quiet two days since Thursday's briefing - no major new policy, inspection or funding story broke over the weekend.

The one genuine development: Ofsted published interim findings from an independent evaluation of its own new-look inspection framework on Friday, broadly positive but flagging workload as still unresolved.
Nothing new locally in Sheffield or South Yorkshire in the last 48 hours - today's diary items below are the main things on leaders' radar this fortnight.

diary.text: Midday deadline for Sheffield secondary school applications for September 2027 entry (national deadline 31 Oct).
Extended deadline for schools to complete autumn census free school meals eligibility rechecks.

sections.heading: Ofsted & accountability: interim evaluation finds inspections landing better, but workload still a worry

items.lede: Friday's independently-commissioned interim evaluation of Ofsted's renewed inspection framework found most inspected providers rate the experience positively so far.
items.body: IFF Research's interim findings, covering the first four survey waves since the new framework and report cards launched, found 88% of inspected providers agreed their inspection was conducted respectfully, 76% collaboratively and 78% empathetically, and 81% said their report card accurately described what it's like to be a pupil or learner there. Workload and wellbeing remain flagged as ongoing pressures, though most respondents said inspectors took steps to reduce stress on the day.
items.source: GOV.UK - Independent research finds Ofsted's new-look inspections are more collaborative and respectful, 9 October 2026
items.action: Useful to share with staff anxious about inspection day - the evidence suggests the new approach is landing better than the old single-word judgements, even if workload concerns haven't gone away.

box.text: of providers said their Ofsted inspection under the new framework was conducted respectfully - though workload pressure remains a live concern.
